provenance.source: Y. Kim, A. Eddins, S. Anand, K. X. Wei, E. van den Berg, S. Rosenblatt, H. Nayfeh, Y. Wu, M. Zaletel, K. Temme, A. Kandala, "Evidence for the utility of quantum computing before fault tolerance", Nature 618, 500-505 (2023)
provenance.checked: The published-version PDF (UC eScholarship mirror of the Nature article; nature.com itself requires cookie auth and refuses automated fetch) and the Supplementary Information PDF were both fetched and text-extracted. The operator supports are printed as the Fig. 3 / Fig. 4 panel titles, e.g. Fig. 3b's title is the literal string "<X13,29,31 Y9,30 Z8,12,17,28,32>"; the per-observable `source_detail` below quotes the panel title it was read from. The main text and PubMed Central copy (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10266970/) were cross-read for the accompanying definitions and Clifford eigenvalues.

provenance.qubit_indexing: IBM Eagle device numbering 0..126. The experiment ran on ibm_kyiv; this repo's lattice comes from the ibm_sherbrooke (FakeSherbrooke) coupling map. No fetched source asserts the two index maps are identical, but the `verification` note below closes that gap computationally: the published supports are reproduced exactly on the Sherbrooke map, including the weight-17 operator whose 5-step causal cone covers 68 qubits.
provenance.verification: Every entry with a `stabilizer_origin` is reproduced by this repo's own engine, not merely transcribed: propagating the seed observable forward through `circuits.heavy_hex_kicked_ising(127, trotter_steps, theta_h=pi/2, order='x-then-zz')` yields a single Pauli string whose support and sign equal the `support` and `clifford_eigenvalue` recorded here. This is checked by `test_published_supports_are_reproduced_by_the_stabilizer_relation` in `python/paulistrings/tests/test_examples_circuits.py`. It simultaneously validates the support transcription, the heavy-hex edge list, the Trotter layer order, and the ibm_kyiv/ibm_sherbrooke index correspondence.

circuit.theta_zz_note: theta_J = -pi/2, verbatim from the paper: "For experimental simplicity, we focus on the case theta_J = -2*J*dt = -pi/2 such that the ZZ rotation requires only one CNOT". In this repo's exp(-i*theta*P/2) convention that same angle is theta_zz = -pi/2, realizing exp(+i*(pi/4)*Z_i Z_j).
circuit.layer_order_note: Supplementary Information Eq. (4) writes one Trotter layer as U(theta_h) = prod_{<i,j>} R_{Z_i Z_j}(-pi/2) * prod_i R_{X_i}(theta_h); the rightmost factor acts first, so the X layer precedes the ZZ layer.
circuit.theta_h_sweep_note: The paper states only "theta_h is swept between 0 and pi/2" and gives no explicit grid. Begusic, Gray & Chan (arXiv:2308.05077) report increments of pi/32 for their comparison data.

light_cone_sizes.note: Supplementary Information section VII B; after the paper's depth reduction these become <= 19, 26 and 48.

weight_1_z62.source_detail: Fig. 4b panel title is the literal string "<Z62>". Main text: "we extend the circuit depth to 20 Trotter steps (60 CNOT layers) and estimate the theta_h dependence of a weight-1 observable, <Z62>, in Fig. 4b, in which the causal cone extends over the entire device", and "we choose an observable that obtains the expected result <Z62> = 1 at the verifiable theta_h = 0 point". Note Fig. 3a's weight-1 case is instead the 127-qubit average magnetization Mz, not Z62.

weight_10.source_detail: Fig. 3b panel title is the literal string "<X13,29,31 Y9,30 Z8,12,17,28,32>". Main text: "Fig. 3b,c show weight-10 and weight-17 observables. The latter operators are stabilizers of the Clifford circuit at theta_h = pi/2, obtained by evolution of the initial stabilizers Z13 and Z58, respectively, of |0>^127 for five Trotter steps". Supplementary Information section VII: "the three observables considered in the Figure 3 can all be expressed in this way: weight-1 Zk = Z(0, k), weight-10 stabilizer Z(5, 13), and weight-17 stabilizer Z(5, 58)". Eigenvalue from the Fig. 3 caption: "The weight-10 and weight-17 observables in b and c are stabilizers of the circuit at theta_h = pi/2 with respective eigenvalues +1 and -1; all values in c have been negated for visual simplicity."

weight_17.source_detail: Fig. 3c panel title is the literal string "<X37,41,52,56,57,58,62,79 Y75 Z38,40,42,63,72,80,90,91>". This is Z(5, 58) of Supplementary Information section VII. Clifford eigenvalue -1 per the Fig. 3 caption (quoted under weight_10); the caption also warns that Fig. 3c's plotted values are negated for display, so the literal Pauli string with coefficient +1 -- what this entry encodes -- is the operator, not the plotted quantity.

weight_17_modified.source_detail: Fig. 4a panel title is the literal string "<X37,41,52,56,57,58,62,79 Y38,40,42,63,72,80,90,91 Z75>". DISTINCT FROM weight_17: identical X support, but the Y and Z sets are swapped -- the RX(pi/2) conjugate. Main text: "The first example (Fig. 4a) is similar to Fig. 3c but with a further final layer of single-qubit Pauli rotations". Supplementary Information: "the modified weight-17 operator measured in Figure 4(a) is Z~(5, 58) with the modified state |Psi~(5, theta)>. This is equivalent to measuring Z(6, 58) with state |Psi(6, theta)>". Confusing this operator with weight_17 gives a silently wrong observable of the same weight and the same X support.

reference_values.note: Kim et al.'s own experimental values with error bars live in the paper's dataset at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.22500355 ("The datasets generated and analysed during this study are available at..."), which refuses automated fetch. Converged exact benchmarks for all four observables, on a theta_h grid of pi/32, are published by Begusic, Gray & Chan at https://github.com/tbegusic/arxiv-2308.05077-data (exact.csv; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10223349). Neither has been fetched into this repo yet; benchmark C's reference is to be loaded through `examples/common/oracles.py::load_published_reference` with its own provenance header, or self-converged per plan decision D5. No expectation value is recorded here so that nothing in this file can be mistaken for a verified reference number.
